quiz.q: Why are bolts tightened in a star pattern?
quiz.correct: So the flange closes evenly instead of tilting

quiz.q: What can happen if a bolt gets far too much torque?
quiz.correct: The thread strips or the bolt yields
wrong: Nothing, the joint just gets heavier

quiz.q: Why does a rocket drop its empty stages?
quiz.correct: To stop carrying dead weight

quiz.q: A rocket has a thrust-to-weight ratio of 0.8. What happens?
quiz.correct: It stays on the pad

quiz.q: What does doubling a stage's propellant do to its delta-v?
quiz.correct: It rises, but by less than double

quiz.q: A higher specific impulse means...
quiz.correct: More push from each kilogram of propellant

quiz.q: What is max-Q?
quiz.correct: The moment of highest aerodynamic pressure
wrong: The end of the engine burn

quiz.q: Why does the rocket tip over after liftoff?
quiz.correct: Orbit needs sideways speed, not just height
wrong: To save fuel on the pad

quiz.q: Why launch towards the east?
quiz.correct: The ground already moves east, giving a free speed boost

quiz.q: You are in orbit when the periapsis...
quiz.correct: Stays above the atmosphere

quiz.q: Why does a satellite need a battery?
quiz.correct: Solar panels make no power in Earth's shadow

quiz.q: Why keep each eclipse to a shallow depth of discharge?
quiz.correct: A battery lasts thousands of orbits that way
wrong: Deep discharge is not allowed in space

quiz.q: What does the EPS do?
quiz.correct: Collects solar power, charges the battery and feeds the boards

quiz.q: What keeps a CubeSat switched off inside its dispenser?
quiz.correct: A deployment switch held down by the dispenser rails

quiz.q: What happens if the Remove-Before-Flight pin is left in?
quiz.correct: The satellite never wakes up
wrong: The satellite is extra safe in orbit

quiz.q: A pyro cable is missing. What happens at that event?
quiz.correct: It does not fire: the stage or fairing stays attached

quiz.q: When is the Safe/Arm plug switched to ARMED?
quiz.correct: Late in the countdown, at the pad
wrong: Whenever people work on the wiring

quiz.q: What is telemetry?
quiz.correct: Measurements a vehicle radios to the ground

quiz.q: Which gives sharper pointing for a high-resolution camera?
quiz.correct: Reaction wheels with a star tracker

quiz.q: A smaller ground sample distance means...
quiz.correct: More detail in each pixel

quiz.q: When can a satellite send data to a ground station?
quiz.correct: Only while the station can see it

quiz.q: The camera makes more data than the radio can send. What happens?
quiz.correct: Storage fills up and new images are lost
wrong: The camera turns itself off safely

quiz.q: How many times did a Saturn V fly?
What did the F-1 engine burn?
quiz.correct: Kerosene and liquid oxygen

quiz.q: What made the S-IVB's J-2 engine special?
quiz.correct: It could restart in space
wrong: It was the biggest engine ever built

quiz.q: What did Rehbar-I release to let scientists track upper-atmosphere winds?
quiz.correct: A sodium cloud

quiz.q: What did flight controller John Aaron suggest to bring telemetry back?
quiz.correct: Switch the SCE to AUX

quiz.q: Landsat satellites have photographed Earth's land since...
